Roles, work items, messages, progress and history for teams of [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and Claude Code agents, on **one append-only ledger**.

A team of agents usually coordinates through prose: role files that the model has to remember, status tables that someone has to type, and messages that nobody can prove were sent. This plugin turns that into data.

- An agent says "I am ready" by calling a tool. The plugin records the event, checks the pull request, tells the right peer, counts the deadline and updates the board.

- **The role is bound to the agent you pick in OpenCode.** It comes from the session's agent id on the first turn and stays: switching the agent inside the session does not change it (the attempt is recorded), and a subagent never holds a role, whatever agent it runs. So the model each role uses is the one you configured for that agent.
- **CLI identity is declared, not proven.** A name holds only the role the profile's `cli` block grants it, is refused for any name that belongs to an OpenCode session, and cannot change role later. This is a guard against mistakes, not a security boundary: see [Who can hold a role](#who-can-hold-a-role).
- **No archive of a very large ledger yet.** Nothing is ever pruned; archiving a closed database file is planned.
- **GitHub is polled** through the `gh` CLI every `syncMinutes`; a failure is recorded and changes nothing.
- Generated pages are written only by `coordination render` unless `render.auto` is set, so your working tree is not touched behind your back.
- Do not run it next to `agent-mail`.

The mode creates no agents and changes no models or permissions.
It does not bypass holds, parked fronts, file overlap checks or owner approvals.
Without useful authorized work, the PM must define a useful next item or seek the required approval.
A blocker report does not close the cycle; the timer continues until an action satisfies the check or the owner disables the mode.
The mode never authorizes invented work or removal of a safety hold just to satisfy its activity check.
The OpenCode server must stay active; this timer cannot restart a stopped process or wake a CLI identity.

Roles, work items, messages, progress and history for teams of [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and Claude Code agents, on **one append-only ledger**.

A team of agents usually coordinates through prose: role files that the model has to remember, status tables that someone has to type, and messages that nobody can prove were sent. This plugin turns that into data.

- An agent says "I am ready" by calling a tool. The plugin records the event, checks the pull request, tells the right peer, counts the deadline and updates the board.

|---|---|
| **Communication** | Typed messages with record ids, deadlines the plugin follows (re-sent after one block, escalated after two), delivery into the other session, a bridge to Claude Code sessions. |
| **Work control** | Items with a life cycle (proposed → accepted → ready → assigned → in progress → in review → merged → measured → validated), assignment checks (file overlap, one open item per engineer, holds and freezes), fresh-session assignment, handover and reassignment. |
| **Progress control** | The board (now / next / later per front), measures with their records, bets with prediction and result, stalls detected by the clock, a generated state digest and owner bundle. |
| **History** | One SQLite ledger per repository: append-only (the database refuses UPDATE and DELETE), reproducible (`rebuild` replays every projection from the events), queryable (`history`, `record`, `export`). |
| **Less documentation** | `ACTIVE`, board, roadmap, status and a JSON snapshot are rendered from the ledger; `coordination render --check` fails on a stale or hand-edited page. |

- **Non-invasive.** Agetor installs no hooks and no MCP server, and it doesn't edit your `CLAUDE.md`. It drives the real CLI the way you would.
- **Restart-safe.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode run inside `tmux`, so quitting Agetor doesn't stop them, and the next launch reconnects to them. fx and Cursor are the exceptions: each runs as a child process of Agetor, talking the Agent Client Protocol over stdio, so a turn in progress doesn't survive a restart and can't be reattached. fx stops when Agetor quits.

## Features

**The harness orchestrator.**
A local-first kanban for running Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, fx, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode in parallel, with each task in its own git worktree. [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/alamops/agetor?style=flat-square&label=release&color=4c1)](https://github.com/alamops/agetor/releases/latest) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-Apple%20Silicon-111?style=flat-square&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](#install) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/alamops/agetor?style=flat-square&color=blue)](./LICENSE)

### Stay in the loop

- **Notifications.** Native macOS notifications link straight to the task that needs you. Cards show an unread dot when the agent has said something new.
- **Usage meter.** Plan quota for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor accounts, read with the logins those CLIs already have, plus local token rollups.
- **Themes and automatic updates.** Auto, dark or light theme. The app is signed, notarized and updates itself in place.

- **Local-first.** Everything runs on your machine. There's no Agetor account, no cloud relay and no telemetry.
- **Non-invasive.** Agetor installs no hooks and no MCP server, and it doesn't edit your `CLAUDE.md`. It drives the real CLI the way you would.
- **Restart-safe.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode run inside `tmux`, so quitting Agetor doesn't stop them, and the next launch reconnects to them. fx and Cursor are the exceptions: each runs as a child process of Agetor, talking the Agent Client Protocol over stdio, so a turn in progress doesn't survive a restart and can't be reattached. fx stops when Agetor quits.

---

- **One local API.** The desktop UI and the CLI both talk to the core over HTTP and Server-Sent Events. The API listens only on `127.0.0.1`, and every route except `/health` requires a random token generated at each launch. There are two such tokens: the app's own webview uses one that is never written to disk, and the `agetor` CLI uses a weaker one that is (see [Security model](#security-model)).
- **Drive the real CLI; don't re-implement it.** Claude Code runs as an interactive session inside `tmux` and receives prompts as keystrokes. Its structured output comes from the transcript Claude writes itself. Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and GitHub Copilot run once per turn inside `tmux` and resume by session id. OpenCode 2 runs on a server Agetor starts for each harness (itself inside `tmux`), and OpenCode 1.x runs once per turn inside `tmux`. fx and Cursor talk the Agent Client Protocol to a child process of Agetor, and Cursor resumes by session id too.
- **Restart-safe by design.** On boot, Agetor reattaches to any `tmux`-hosted session that is still alive and replays its transcript without duplicates. Runs whose session is gone move back to **Ready**, so no card is left stuck in Running.
- **Local persistence.** Tasks, runs, events, projects, harnesses and preferences live in a SQLite database with versioned migrations.

Mozzie is a local-first desktop app that turns AI coding agents into a managed workforce. You describe what needs building — Mozzie breaks it into work items, spins up isolated git worktrees, assigns agents, manages dependencies, and queues everything for your review. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, or your own scripts — as many agents running in parallel as your machine can handle. One window. One diff review. One merge.

If you want a personal build team that runs on your machine with zero cloud dependency, this is it.

### 🌐 Multi-agent collaboration

## 语义所有权

以下语义必须由 ZAgenticOPN 自有，不能委托给候选项目：

| ZAgenticOPN 语义 | 必须保持的事实 |

| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | 稳定身份 | `Human → device → agent_instance`；session 是一次运行，不是新主体。 |
| R2 | Agent private context | 保存私有协作摘要、未发布观察和恢复引用；不等于完整对话或知识库。 |
| R3 | shared coordination context | 明确发布、按 Initiative/project 隔离；Git 保存 durable engineering facts。 |
| R4 | 发布 available work | Work Item 可独立 claim，具有 objective、acceptance 和 references。 |
| R5 | 发现 shared frontier | Human 触发后，Agent 查询并选择自己 eligible 的工作；不含自动发现。 |
